findings.title: A 9-wei V1 DOLA stake makes the cutover's per-user loss post-condition revert: the fixed 2-wei slack is smaller than autoDOLA's round-trip rounding, so dust can stall the cutover the story says it cannot
findings.description: Story 082 AC5 asks for "invariants that ensure dust cannot grief (revert/stall) the cutover". The dust predicate (`_depositWouldFail`) only asks whether the V2 deposit would REVERT. The per-user post-condition then applies a flat 2-wei absolute slack on top of the bps bound. `WEI_SLACK = 2` (CutoverStableStakerV2Mainnet.s.sol:109), and the ERC4626 bps term is `pre * 2 / 10_000`, which is 0 for any position under 5,000 wei. A small position goes through three floors: its V1 `stake` credit (`convertToAssets(previewDeposit)`), the exit credit (`amt*R/P`), and the V2 re-deposit credit (`convertToAssets(shares)`). On autoDOLA, where one share is worth about 1.19 DOLA-wei (totalAssets 55113967399722755135519 / totalSupply 46317440394398677974688), that round trip loses 3 wei. The planner classifies the position as MIGRATABLE, because the deposit does not revert. The post-condition then reverts. V1 is Active and unpaused until the run's own Phase 1, so anyone can plant such a position at any time for 9 wei of DOLA plus gas.
findings.impact: The whole cutover (preview AND the broadcast's local pass) reverts at `cutover-post: cutover lost more principal than the strategy can explain` on the first pool. It keeps reverting on every re-run for as long as the planted position exists. The position cannot be removed except by migrating it, and migrating it is exactly what trips the check. The only way forward is a code or constant change. No funds are at risk: the revert fires in forge's local pass before any transaction is sent. The harm is a permissionless, near-free stall of a mainnet operation, which the story explicitly promised could not happen.
findings.evidence: Code (StableStakerCutoverCore.sol:452-455): `require(pre - post <= pre * maxLossBps / CUTOVER_MAX_BPS + weiSlack, "cutover-post: cutover lost more principal than the strategy can explain");` with `uint256 public constant WEI_SLACK = 2;` and `ERC4626_MAX_LOSS_BPS = 2`. Fork @25975869 (fork-logs/h-F.log): exhaustive search over stake inputs 1..400 wei -> `DUSTSEARCH|DOLA|worstStakeInput=9|worstLossWei=3|countAboveBound=63`, while autoUSDC gives `worstLossWei=2|countAboveBound=0`. Live PoC (fork-logs/h-G.log, test_G_plantedDolaDustStallsCutover): griefer `V1.stake(DOLA, 9)` -> `planted V1 DOLA principal (wei) 8` -> full `run()` in PREVIEW_MODE -> `PLANTED_DUST|cutover REVERTED| cutover-post: cutover lost more principal than the strategy can explain`. Also at mainnet state today: USDC dust users of 12/22/30/66/86/90 wei each lose exactly 2 wei, sitting on the slack boundary (fork-logs/h-A-users-events.log).
findings.severityRationale: Story-violating and permissionless, but fail-closed. It reverts in the local pass before any broadcast, and nothing is lost. The operator is present and can fix it with a one-constant edit. The impact is on operational availability, not on assets, so it does not meet Medium.
findings.recommendation: Derive the absolute slack from the destination vault, not a constant, e.g. `weiSlack = 2 + ceil(vault.convertToAssets(1)) + 1` (share-price rounding on both floors), or add the planner's own predicted loss (`amount - convertToAssets(previewDeposit(amount*R/P))`) to the bound for that user. Alternatively classify positions whose predicted round-trip loss exceeds the bound as allow-listed stragglers under the existing 1-cent cap. Add a regression to test/StableStakerCutoverDust.t.sol that plants a 9-wei DOLA-shaped position on a vault with share price > 1.

findings.title: The post-broadcast `:preview` 'verification' re-executes any outstanding step under prank instead of asserting it is already done, so a partial or diverged mainnet cutover verifies green
findings.description: The package.json doc key and the story both claim that after a broadcast, `:preview` "re-runs every assertion and smoke test against the live deployment", with every phase detecting "from on-chain state that it is done and skips". In fact every phase is `if (!done) do();`. Preview impersonates OWNER, so any step that did NOT land on mainnet is silently performed inside the simulation, and Phase 8 then asserts the simulated state. Nothing in preview mode, not even with a progress file loaded, requires that zero mutations were needed. The per-user loss bound is also evaluated only over `plan.migratable` from the same leg, which is empty after a broadcast, so the on-chain credits are never re-checked. This is the run-22 `ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast` family: all planning and assertions run in forge's local pass, and the batches are frozen there, before the Ledger session sends ~47 transactions with `--slow --skip-simulation`. A V1 `stake` that lands after the local pass but before the Phase-1 `pause()` transaction (cf. ledger c04da307336c on promotion-ready) is absent from every batch. Phase 7 then revokes V1's phUSD mint anyway, which bricks that user's `userMigrate` while their frozen pending is non-zero. The chained preview then migrates them in simulation and reports success.
findings.impact: The operator's only automated outcome check can report a finished cutover while mainnet has V1 phUSD mint still live, V2 still paused, or a staker stranded on V1 behind a revoked mint. Remedies exist (owner re-grant plus re-run), but nothing surfaces the need for them. No direct loss is proven. Mainnet per-user loss stays bounded by the strategies' own minOut floors.
findings.evidence: Code: Phase 7 `if (_canMintPhUSD(STABLE_STAKER_V1)) { IPhUSDOwner(PHUSD).setMinter(STABLE_STAKER_V1, false); ... }` and `if (v2.paused()) v2.unpause();`, both executed under `vm.startPrank(OWNER)` in preview. Per-user check loop `for (uint256 i = 0; i < plan.migratable.length; i++)` (Core:440). Fork @25975869, harness inheriting the unmodified script: (C) after a full cutover, `phUSD.setMinter(V1,true)` (revoke 'did not land') then `run()` in PREVIEW_MODE -> `[PASS] ... MASK_REVOKE|preview run() PASSED although V1 phUSD mint was live on-chain` (log shows 'REVOKED' again, fork-logs/h-test_C_previewMasksMissingRevoke.log). (C2) Pauser pauses V2 ('unpause did not land') then `run()` -> `MASK_PAUSED_V2|preview run() PASSED although V2 was paused on-chain`. The console output is byte-identical to a clean verification ('V1 pauser -> Pauser and V1 unpaused (inert); V2 + Antimatter registered with Pauser; V2 unpaused'), fork-logs/h-test_C2_previewMasksPausedV2.log.
findings.severityRationale: It degrades a compensating control and does not open an exploit. Every masked state is recoverable by the trusted owner in 1-2 transactions. The stranded-staker limb needs a stake inside a short pre-pause window. This fits the precedent run-22 L-level members of the same family, and M-01 there stood only because no verification existed at all.
findings.recommendation: Add a verify-only mode. When `isPreview` and the progress file has `deploymentStatus == completed`, run `_phase8_wiringAssertions()` plus live-state asserts (V1 stakerCount/totalStaked == 0 per pool, V2 unpaused, V1 mint revoked) BEFORE `vm.startPrank`, and make every phase `require(alreadyDone, "verify: step X not on chain")` instead of performing it. Persist the per-user pre-migration principals (or the V1 MigratedOut/V2 DepositedFor receipts) and re-check the loss bound from on-chain V2 userInfo. Also fold the planning snapshot's staker set into the progress file and assert that V1 stakerCount at the pause transaction equals it.

findings.title: The cutover hands V2's and Antimatter's only pause authority to a global Pauser whose `pause()` loop already reverts `EnforcedPause` on two pre-paused registered contracts; Phase 8 asserts registration, not a working breaker
findings.description: Phase 7's own NatSpec states the invariant it relies on: "`Pauser.pause()` loops `pause()` over every registered contract with no try/catch, and OZ `_pause` reverts on an already-paused contract, so a paused registered V1 would brick the protocol-wide emergency pause." It therefore unpauses V1, sets `v2.setPauser(PAUSER)` and `antimatter.setPauser(PAUSER)`, and registers both. On mainnet today, two registered contracts are already paused: index 2 `0x3984eBC84d45a889dDAc595d13dc0aC2E54819F4` and index 4 `0xf5F91E8240a0320CAC40b799B25F944a61090E5B`. So the loop reverts before it reaches V1 (index 18), V2 (28) or Antimatter (29). After Phase 7, `StableStakerV2.pause()` is `onlyPauser`, so OWNER cannot pause V2 without first sending `setPauser(OWNER)`. Story Decision 9 flagged the pre-paused contracts for 'human attention', but at 1c1608c the script neither checks nor handles them, and Phase 8's 'pausers registered' assertion passes regardless.
findings.impact: After the cutover, the permissionless EYE-burn emergency stop is non-functional for every registered contract. That includes the new V2, which custodies all migrated principal (~5.75k USD across 29 positions), and Antimatter, whose `annihilate` mints unbacked phUSD. Incident response falls back to the Ledger owner sending 2 transactions per contract. The condition existed before the cutover, but this script extends it to the two new contracts, and its own rationale assumes the breaker works.
findings.evidence: Fork @25975869 after a full cutover (fork-logs/h-B.log): EYE-funded actor `Pauser.pause()` -> `PAUSER_LOOP|REVERTED|0xd93c0665` (EnforcedPause()); per-contract prank-as-Pauser `pause()`: `PAUSE_ONE|2|0x3984eBC84d45a889dDAc595d13dc0aC2E54819F4|REVERT|0xd93c0665`, `PAUSE_ONE|4|0xf5F91E8240a0320CAC40b799B25F944a61090E5B|REVERT|0xd93c0665`, all other 28 incl. `|18|0xbce8...(V1)|ok`, `|28|0x8482...(V2)|ok`, `|29|0x10EB...(Antimatter)|ok`; `OWNER_PAUSE_V2|REVERT| StableStaker: only pauser`. Live `cast call` confirms `paused()==true, pauser()==Pauser` for both at the fork block. Phase 8 checks only `IPauserRegistry(PAUSER).isRegistered(address(v2))` / `(address(antimatter))`.
findings.severityRationale: The condition is pre-existing and owner-remediable (unpause, or setPauser away and unregister, the two stale contracts). No exploit is enabled by itself; it removes a defence-in-depth control. It is a non-obvious footgun: the script's own comments show the author believes the loop is live.
findings.recommendation: Before (or as part of) the cutover, remediate the registry: either unpause `0x3984eBC8…` and `0xf5F91E82…`, or `setPauser` them away and `Pauser.unregister` them. Add a Phase 0/8 check that iterates `Pauser.getPausableContracts()` and requires `!paused()` for each, or in preview simulates `Pauser.pause()` from an EYE-funded prank inside a `snapshotState/revertToState`, so that 'registered' means 'actually pausable'.

findings.title: The '067 floor' post-condition compares two numbers that are booked identically, so it cannot fail; story-067's zero-haircut anchor on the pre-migration booked total is not implemented
findings.description: Story 082 Phase 6 asks for "realized >= booked principal (067)", and story-067 defines that floor as realized principal versus the PRE-migration booked total (`principalOf(...) >= savedPreMigBookedDola`). The script instead asserts `strategy.principalOf(token, V2) >= V2.totalStaked` after migration. Both sides are credited with the same `credited` value in every `depositFor` (the strategy books `clientBalances[V2] += credited`, and V2 books `totalStaked += credited`), so the check holds with equality by construction and cannot detect a haircut. The executor's review carried this forward as a non-blocking Low, and the NatSpec, comment and revert string still call it the 067 floor. The real loss protection is the per-user bound, which was itself relaxed from the story's 0 bps + 2 wei to 2 bps + 2 wei (ERC4626) and 61 bps (USDe) by Decision 4. Same class as ledger YS-32 523ef3df52a6, where the story-067 floor measures the wrong quantity on migrate:ys-swap-cleanup.
findings.impact: A reader or operator relies on a named safety gate that provides no protection. The aggregate pre-to-post principal change (USDe -8.934 USDe, USDC -0.170245, DOLA -0.00415) is never checked against any aggregate floor. Only per-user bps bounds apply, and they are looser than the story planned.
findings.evidence: Code (Core:469-471): `uint256 realized = ICutoverStrategy(strategy).principalOf(token, address(v2)); require(realized >= v2Staked, "cutover-post: strategy principal for V2 < V2 booked totalStaked (067 floor)");`. Fork @25975869 POSTPOOL (fork-logs/h-A-users-events.log): DOLA `v2Staked=1222723447469613917495|principalOfV2=1222723447469613917495`, USDC `1968305934|1968305934`, USDe `2557881617164101522200|2557881617164101522200`, all exactly equal. Story 067 text: `ysDolaV2.principalOf(DOLA, ORIGINAL_STABLE_STAKER) >= savedPreMigBookedDola`.
findings.severityRationale: This is a spec-conformance and assurance gap on an attended script. The per-user bounds still stop a real vault loss, so there is no asset impact.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with a real aggregate gate anchored on the snapshot: require `V2.totalStaked_after >= P * (MAX_BPS - maxLossBps) / MAX_BPS - n * WEI_SLACK`, where P is `V1.migrationInfo(token).principalSnapshot`. Alternatively rename the check (for example 'V2 book/strategy lockstep') so it is not presented as the 067 floor, and record the Decision-4 relaxation as a human-accepted deviation.

dedup.uniquenessVsSiblings: A tautology: both sides are booked from the same credited value. Distinct from SSV2C-01 (slack too tight), SSV2C-02 (preview self-heal) and SSV2C-05 (who bears the loss). SSV2C-05 cites the missing aggregate check only as context. Its fix (a top-up, or owner acceptance) does not repair the floor, and SSV2C-04's fix (a real aggregate floor) does not change the allocation.

findings.title: Cutover loss is borne by stakers (USDe 34.8 bps, 8.93 USDe) while protocol-held value several times larger stays with the protocol: V1 idle buffers left on V1, story-060 surplus relinquished, and the USDe booking haircut accrues as strategy surplus
findings.description: Owner migration intent (2026-08-28) says: sweep yield AND the set-aside buffer into principal, relinquish over-credit to the protocol, safe > precise, and 'err toward the USER where possible'. The cutover follows the relinquish leg (story 082 background, story-060 surplus) but none of the user-favouring legs. Frozen V1 excludes its idle buffer from R (known and preserved in V1), and the script leaves those buffers on V1 for a later owner `rescueERC20` (Decision 14). Every migrating staker therefore takes the full exit-plus-re-entry haircut. On USDe the V2 re-deposit books `credit * (1 - 30 bps)` while the swap delivered more, so part of the users' loss immediately becomes strategy surplus attributable to V2 and skimmable by the protocol. Story-060's documented purpose for the DOLA/USDC surplus ('absorbs ... small realized losses in any future terminal migration (R reaches P before users take a haircut)') is also not realized. The memo's intent #2 supersedes that purpose, but story 082 does not say so.
findings.impact: Users lose USDe 8.933848235898477800 (34.805 bps, every holder), USDC 0.170245 (0.865 bps), DOLA 0.004154983888567955 (0.034 bps). Over the same window the protocol keeps 49.845539781409382100 USDe, 10.430694 USDC and 6.997032072106485771 DOLA of idle V1 buffer, plus 26.898455742910213445 DOLA and 27.043385 USDC of relinquished surplus. After migration, V2's `totalBalanceOf - principalOf` shows 4.136480965658327219 USDe, 4.326353 USDC and 2.664877367748603061 DOLA of immediately skimmable surplus. Amounts are small, and the relaxed per-user bounds are disclosed (Decision 4).
findings.severityRationale: About 9 USD of user loss, fully disclosed, with no exploit. The finding is a Law-2 allocation mismatch against the owner-intent memo, raised for human disposition. Owner 'safe > precise' may justify accepting it.
findings.recommendation: Either record explicit owner acceptance in story 082 (that users bear the cutover haircut and buffers go to the protocol), or add an optional Phase 7b top-up. `rescueERC20` the V1 idle buffer to OWNER, temporarily `v2.setMigrator(OWNER)`, `depositFor(user, pre - post)` for each migrated user (bounded by the rescued buffer, noting that the USDe top-up is itself haircut 30 bps), then `v2.setMigrator(address(0))`. At minimum, amend story 082 to state where the story-060 surplus goes and why its story-060 purpose no longer applies.

findings.title: The story-080 DeployMocks rehearsal omits the Antimatter phUSD mint grant that the mainnet script proves load-bearing, and the local verifier never calls autoAnnihilate, so the rehearsal cannot exercise V2's only reward path
findings.description: Story 082 names DeployMocks' `_deployAntimatterAndStableStakerV2` + `_rehearseStableStakerCutover` as 'THE TEMPLATE for ordering and assertions'. The mainnet script adds `phUSD.setMinter(antimatter, true)` (Decision 3), because `Antimatter.annihilate` pays its antimatter half with `_phUSD.mint(recipient, amount)`. The executor showed with a negative control that autoAnnihilate otherwise reverts `phUSD: caller is not authorized to mint`. DeployMocks grants only `antimatter.setApprovedMinter(V2)` and `phUSD.setMinter(V2)`. Its local phUSD is `MockPhUSD`, whose `mint` requires `info.canMint && info.mintVersion == mintVersion`. `verify-stable-staker.sh` → `ClaimWithdrawStableStaker.s.sol` asserts `claimEnabled` is false and then withdraws, never calling `autoAnnihilate`. On anvil, the only reward path while `claimEnabled == false` therefore appears to revert, and no local test would notice. Story 082 Decision 3 flagged this as a follow-up, and at 1c1608c it is unfixed.

findings.title: Spec deviation: the script grants phUSD mint authority to the new Antimatter contract (a third mint grant not in story 082's Phase 5 list) under machine-only approval
findings.description: Story AC4 and Phase 5 list exactly two grants: V2 → Antimatter and V2 → phUSD. The script adds `phUSD.setMinter(Antimatter, true)`, gated by `GRANT_ANTIMATTER_PHUSD_MINT = true`. The Law-1 check passes. `Antimatter` mints phUSD only inside `annihilate`, at exactly the antimatter amount the caller burns. The approved Antimatter minter set is asserted to be exactly {V2} (`approvedMinterCount() == 1`), and the phUSD candidate mask moves only by the V1 bit (511→510), with mintVersion unchanged. The new unbacked-issuance channel is therefore bounded by V2 emissions (2.1 × V1's phUSD rate, per story AC3) plus OWNER mints. That is Antimatter's accepted design (1 AM = 1 unbacked phUSD), and memory ss18l1's wont-fix covers the top-up. The story sits in `auto-complete/` with 'machine approval — not human-reviewed', and its review carried this forward as '[medium] ... the human should be aware before broadcast'. It is filed here so the human sees it in the audit channel.
findings.impact: A new mainnet contract gains phUSD mint authority without an explicit human sign-off in the story. No exploit path was found: annihilate burns the caller's own AM one-for-one, and AM minting is restricted to V2 and the owner.
findings.evidence: Code: `bool public constant GRANT_ANTIMATTER_PHUSD_MINT = true;` ... `IPhUSDOwner(PHUSD).setMinter(address(antimatter), true);`. Antimatter.sol:293-294 `_phUSD.mint(recipient, amount);`. Fork preview: `phUSD.setMinter(Antimatter) - VERIFIED at current mintVersion`, `phUSD minter delta OK (live mask / V1 revoked): 510 true`, Phase 8 `approvedMinterCount() == 1` passed; phUSD supply delta during cutover = +85.471458401387198196 = exactly the sum of V1 pending rewards (no other mint).
findings.severityRationale: A disclosed and necessary deviation with the authority increase bounded and asserted. It is raised for human disposition only.
findings.recommendation: Record a human sign-off for the Antimatter phUSD grant in story 082 (or a follow-up story) before broadcast, and note in the Phase 8 NatSpec that the grant's issuance is bounded by `approvedMinterCount()==1` plus the V2 rate.
